title: Stewardship Field Journal: Cross-Functional Microrelease Rituals (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a living field journal capturing operational rituals, lightweight telemetry probes, and cross-functional commitments for small-batch LLM microreleases (microreleases = scoped feature toggles, model swaps, routing changes <=1% traffic slices). Goal: make launches predictable, fast to revert, and psychologically safe for product, infra, SRE, and research.

High-level principles (short):
- Small, observable changes: prefer many tiny gated activations over a single big switch.
- Human-led stewardship: each microrelease has a named Steward (product) and an Oncall Partner (SRE/infra) responsible for immediate decisions.
- Fast feedback loops: 5-minute telemetry probes + 1-hour human pulse check.
- Bias for rollback: automated and manual escape hatches must be simpler than complex mitigations.

Roles & responsibilities (compact):
- Steward (Product): owns hypothesis, acceptance criteria, comms, and the initial go/no-go.
- Oncall Partner (SRE): health & latency guard, triggers emergency rollback when automated thresholds fire and human checks confirm.
- Model Owner (Applied ML): monitors quality regressions, sanity-checks prompts/outputs; prepares a compatible fallback model variant.
- Release Steward (Ops): executes traffic slices, confirms observation windows, runs synthetic probes.
- Observability Lead (Console team): ensures dashboards/alerts are visible and shared in the steward channel.

Pre-launch checklist (minimum gating):
- Hypothesis statement (1-2 lines) + acceptance metrics (primary + tolerances).
- Small slice defined and implementable via the console: exact cohort filter or route key.
- Observability board linked: latency, error-rate, token-cost, quality signal(s), user-visible error types.
- Synthetic probe script ready (3 scenarios): smoke, edge-case, adversarial prompt.
- Rollback playbook in code and human-runbook (one-click route swap or feature flag off).
- Stakeholder ping list: steward-channel, infra-oncall, ML-oncall, customer-success (if external impact).

Lightweight telemetry probes (examples, 1-line each):
- 90th pct latency change vs baseline (5m sliding window).
- Per-model token-cost delta (rolling 1h).
- Server errors (5xx) and infra requeues (1m granularity).
- Quality drift probe: % of responses with blank/garbled tokens (from QA heuristics).
- Semantic cue probe: failure rate on 4 canonical prompts (synthetic).

Alerting rules (suggested quick set):
- Immediate (auto rollback candidate): +25% 90p latency OR +3x 5xx rate sustained 3m.
- Degrade (page oncall): quality probe failure >10% in 15m OR token-cost +30% in 1h.
- Informational (slack notif): small deltas for early signal e.g. +10% latency for 5m.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Launch announcement (steward to channel):
  "Launching microrelease <id> -> slice <X%> at <T>. Steward: @morgan. Observability board: <link>. Rollback: /rollback <id>. Oncall partner: @ravi. Acceptance: latency 90p <= +10%, quality probe <= 5% failures. Ping if alerts fire"

- Incident ping (auto to channel):
  "ALERT: microrelease <id> triggered auto-threshold at <T>. Action: hold traffic and assess. Steward: @morgan. Oncall: @ravi. If confirmed, execute rollback command in console: /rollback <id>."

Escalation ladder (fast):
1) Steward assesses within 5 min and posts summary.
2) If auto-threshold persists after human review (10 min total), Oncall executes rollback.
3) If rollback fails or systemic infra issue suspected, page SRE pager rotation and engage platform-engineering runbook.

Rollback decision heuristics (short):
- If automated threshold + human corroboration -> immediate rollback.
- If only quality drift without infra impact and business risk tolerable -> halt additional slices and run probe sweep.
- If token-cost spike without quality/latency impact -> throttle slice and run cost-profile rollback within 1h.

Post-launch lightweight postmortem (to be completed within 48h):
- 1-line outcome (succeeded / rolled back / partial revert).
- Metric highlights (what trended, % change, windows).
- Root cause hypothesis and next steps (3 bullets).
- Ownership for follow-up fixes and ETA.

Sample 5-day microrelease rhythm (template):
- Day -2: Finalize hypothesis, implement feature flag, add synthetic probes, link dashboards.
- Day -1: Dry run in staging with synthetic traffic; invite ML and infra to review.
- Day 0 (launch day): 10% of planned slices in AM (very small), steward posts launch message, check 5m probes for first 30m.
- Day +1: If stable, increase slices incrementally (examples: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5%) with 2h observation windows between jumps.
- Day +2 to +4: Run extended observation, collect product metrics; if no regressions, finalize and mark feature flag as GA.

Operational gotchas (observed in the field):
- Over-instrumenting alerts leads to noise: prefer a few high-signal probes rather than many low-signal rules.
- Human fatigue: rotate Steward role across product teams to avoid single-person bottlenecks.
- Backfill: ensure synthetic probes are recorded and runnable by any engineer (not just the author).

Open questions / experiments to try (lab ideas):
- Weighted adaptive slices: can we automatically expand slices faster when telemetry shows consistent stability? (experiment: +10% speedup with conservative guardrails).
- Quality-first gating: add a semantic-similarity probe as a gating metric for rerank/model-swap launches.
- Psychological-safety checklist: micro-survey after each rollout to capture steward confidence and friction points.

Immediate next steps (what I'll do this week):
- Convert the above telemetry probe list into dashboard templates (observability team ticket).
- Add two Slack templates to the repo for automated launch/rollback messages.
- Pilot the stewardship rotation: assign stewards for next 6 microreleases and collect feedback.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep runbook actions 'reversible' and short (<3 commands).
- Archive synthetic probe results to a central bucket for retrospective analysis.
- Make a one-click rollback visible in console modal (ux ticket).

End of entry.

-- Morgan
(steward field experiments, product console)
